new.s: Who was the founder of the Tuluva dynasty?
new.x: Vira Narasimha, son of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, killed Immadi Narasimha in 1505 and founded the Tuluva dynasty; Narasa Nayaka was only a general and regent.
new.angle: U0121 #3 Tuluva founder; PYQ ye033be9a576 dynasty founder

new.s: Annamacharya, who composed 32,000 kirtanas on Lord Venkateswara, was a contemporary of which Vijayanagara ruler?
new.x: Annamacharya (1408-1503) lived in the time of Saluva Narasimha (1485-91); he died before Krishnadevaraya was crowned in 1509.
new.angle: U0121 #7 Saluva Narasimha - contemporary of Annamacharya

new.s: Who was the rajaguru of Krishnadevaraya?
new.x: The Madhva saint Vyasatirtha (Vyasaraya) was Krishnadevaraya's rajaguru; Purandaradasa was his disciple.
new.angle: PYQ y1e89d439e8b contemporary saints of Krishnadevaraya

new.s: Who among the following, called the father of Carnatic music, was a disciple of Vyasatirtha and a contemporary of Krishnadevaraya?
new.x: Purandaradasa, disciple of Krishnadevaraya's rajaguru Vyasatirtha, lived in Krishnadevaraya's time; Tyagaraja and Kshetrayya came much later.
new.angle: PYQ y1e89d439e8b contemporary of Purandaradasa

new.s: Who among the following poets of Krishnadevaraya's court wrote Bhava Chinta Ratna and Veerasaivamrita in Kannada?
new.x: Mallanarya of Krishnadevaraya's court wrote Bhava Chinta Ratna and Veerasaivamrita in Kannada.
new.angle: U0121 #10 court poets' works -> language

new.s: During the reign of which ruler did the Portuguese traveller Fernao Nuniz visit Vijayanagara?

new.angle: U0121 #17 foreign accounts - Nuniz
